body.heading: Five detectives on duty
paragraphs: Your brain sits in the dark inside your head. It cannot see the garden, hear the birds or feel the grass — not by itself. So it employs five detectives to go out and gather the news: your five senses.
Each detective has one special job, and each one reports back to headquarters — your brain — all day long.

body.heading: Sight and hearing
paragraphs: Detective Sight works through your eyes. Eyes catch light bouncing off everything around you, and your brain builds the picture: colors, shapes, movement, faces. Most of what you know about the world arrives through this detective.
Detective Hearing works through your ears. Sounds are invisible shaking in the air — ears catch the shaking, and your brain turns it into voices, music, thunder and the tiny tap of rain.

body.heading: Smell and taste
paragraphs: Detective Smell works through your nose, catching scent particles floating in the air: bread baking, rain coming, a rose, a warning whiff of something burning.

Detective Taste works through your tongue, and it has five flavors to report: sweet, salty, sour, bitter and savory. Smell and taste are partners — hold your nose while eating and notice how much flavor disappears!

body.heading: Touch — the everywhere detective
paragraphs: Detective Touch works through your skin — and skin is everywhere, making touch the only detective on duty over your whole body. Touch reports soft and rough, hot and cold, smooth and scratchy, gentle and ouch.
Together, the five detectives keep you informed, delighted and safe. A hot stove, a sour berry, a friend's voice calling your name — every one of those arrived by detective delivery.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Close your eyes for ten seconds and listen. How many sounds can your hearing detective count? Now open your eyes — what did sight add?
2. Which sense would you choose to make twice as strong for a day — and what would you do with it?

takeaway: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch are five detectives gathering news for your brain — and together they build your whole experience of the world.
materials: Just you and this page — no materials needed
supervision: A grown-up nearby is recommended for younger readers; the think-and-talk questions work well read aloud together.
safetyNotes: Reading only — no physical activity or materials are involved.
screenFreeExtension: Sense walk: take a short walk and deliberately collect one discovery for each sense — something seen, heard, smelled, touched, and (only if a grown-up says it is safe) tasted.
